title: Package integrity hashes and a literal registry password in one input
summary: A pip requirements file with several --hash=sha256 lines and a private index URL whose userinfo carries a literal synthetic password, and a go.sum excerpt beside a GOPROXY URL whose userinfo carries a synthetic password. Only the password is secret.
rationale: Integrity hashes are public and many in one input; a literal credential sits among them. Two failure modes: a span that stretches over adjacent hashes, and a credential missed because the input looks like a hash list. The span is the password between the first colon of the userinfo and the at-sign, and no hash is in a span. This pairs the digest case with the URL-userinfo reasoning rather than repeating either.

expectation.rationale: Flag the password only. RFC 3986 says applications should not render as clear text any data after the first colon of the userinfo, which places the password; the hash lines are covered by the digest case and are outside every span.

sources.supports: Applications should not render as clear text any data after the first colon in userinfo.
Hashes in a requirements file (--hash=sha256:...) are integrity checks for downloads.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. Every value is synthetic: digests are computed over constructed placeholder text, hosts use the reserved .invalid TLD, nothing was tested against any service. Product masking, action policy and measurement stay with the downstream repositories.
